title: Ukraine: The battle beyond war - European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: An ECFR podcast on Ukraine's second front — domestic legitimacy. Roman Petrov warns that peace decisions taken while elections remain suspended could be legally challenged later; Ukraine's ambassador to Sweden Svitlana Zalishchuk counters that war has raised trust in the state unevenly and that public trust is itself a defence capability, while arguing Ukraine is now a contributor to European defence rather than an aid recipient.

themes.theme: Legitimacy risk around any peace deal

insights.claim: Major decisions on peace with Russia could be challenged later if Ukraine's elections remain suspended, according to EU-law professor Roman Petrov.
insights.so_what: A legal-durability risk investors should attach to any Ukraine settlement, reconstruction contract or territorial arrangement agreed under wartime suspension of elections.
insights.locator: Roman warns that major decisions on peace could be challenged later
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

insights.claim: Ukrainians show extraordinary trust in the armed forces, family and civic networks but far less in politicians, government and bureaucrats — an asymmetry that shapes how any peace settlement or reform programme will be received.
insights.so_what: Institutional trust, not battlefield lines, is the variable that determines whether post-war Ukrainian governance holds.
insights.locator: Ukrainians show extraordinary trust in the Armed Forces
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

insights.claim: Corruption scandals at high level, calls for wartime elections, EU accession roadblocks and possible peace talks are converging into a single question of whether wartime trust can be converted into a state people believe in.
insights.so_what: Frames the near-term Ukrainian political risk set as one compound problem rather than separate headlines.
insights.locator: Now, high-level corruption scandals, calls for wartime elections
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

themes.theme: Contrarian readings of Ukrainian state capacity

insights.claim: Svitlana Zalishchuk pushes back on the low-trust narrative, arguing the war has actually increased trust in the Ukrainian state, though unevenly, and that public trust is itself part of Ukraine's national defence capability.
insights.so_what: If trust is a defence asset rather than a governance liability, Western conditionality that erodes it may be counterproductive — a live argument in aid design.
insights.locator: Svitlana pushes back on the picture of low public trust
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

insights.claim: Ukraine may now be better described as a contributor to European defence than a recipient of military aid.
insights.so_what: Reframes Ukraine from cost centre to supplier in European defence-industrial planning — relevant to drone, munitions and battlefield-tech integration with EU programmes.
insights.locator: Why might Ukraine now be better described as a contributor
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

insights.claim: Fast-tracking EU membership risks turning Ukrainian reform into a superficial “copy-paste” of European laws rather than genuine institutional change.
insights.so_what: A caution that accession speed and reform quality trade off — relevant to anyone pricing the durability of Ukrainian regulatory convergence.
insights.locator: if fast-tracking EU membership risks turning reform
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

insights.claim: The RE-ENGAGE project conducted nearly 600 interviews with Kyiv residents last year, at times moving them into air-raid shelters as alarms sounded across the city.
insights.so_what: Establishes the empirical basis and its limits — a Kyiv-only sample, so caution before generalising to the whole country.
insights.locator: RE-ENGAGE conducted nearly 600 interviews with Kyiv residents
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk

insights.claim: The AfD's historic landslide in eastern Germany is being read in Kyiv by those working on EU accession as directly relevant to Ukraine's path into the union.
insights.so_what: Links German far-right momentum to the accession timetable — a transmission channel from German state elections to Ukraine risk.
insights.locator: How is the far-right AfD’s historic landslide in eastern Germany viewed
insights.speaker: Jessica Hendrick, Roman Petrov, Svitlana Zalishchuk
